title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 26. [The Conclusion of the Poem]
html:
The contents of the fourth prakrama; the fruit of hearing; the number of sargas and verses; Damodara, Advaita and Srivasa praise the book; Murari dances; the date of completion

Verse 1

वृन्दावनस्य गमने भक्तवर्गविलापनम्।
सान्त्वनञ्चापि तेषां वै वर्णितं प्रभुणा कृतम्॥१॥

vṛndāvanasya gamane bhaktavargavilāpanam|
sāntvanañcāpi teṣāṁ vai varṇitaṁ prabhuṇā kṛtam||1||

vrindavanasya — to Vrindavana; gamane — at the departure; bhakta-varga-vilapanam — the lament of the devotees; santvanam — the consolation; cha api — and also; tesham — of them; vai — indeed; varnitam — has been described; prabhuna — by the Prabhu; kritam — given.

1Also described is how the devotees wept when the Lord left for Vrindavana, and how the Prabhu consoled them;

Verse 2

वनपथि क्रमेणैव काशीपुर्याश्च दर्शनम्।
तथा विश्वेश्वरस्यापि तपनादेश्च मेलनम्॥२॥

vanapathi krameṇaiva kāśīpuryāśca darśanam|
tathā viśveśvarasyāpi tapanādeśca melanam||2||

vana-pathi — by the forest path; kramena eva — step by step; kashi-puryah — of the city of Kashi; cha — and; darshanam — the sight; tatha — likewise; vishveshvarasya — of Vishveshvara; api — also; tapana-adeh — with Tapana and others; cha — and; melanam — the meeting.

2the journey by the forest path, Kashi, the darshan of Vishveshvara1 and the meeting with Tapana and others;

Verse 3

प्रयागे माधवदेवदर्शनं यमुनामनु।
अग्रवनरेणुकादिमथुरालोकनं तथा॥३॥

prayāge mādhavadevadarśanaṁ yamunāmanu|
agravanareṇukādimathurālokanaṁ tathā||3||

prayage — at Prayaga; madhava-deva-darshanam — the darshan of Lord Madhava; yamunam anu — along the Yamuna; agravana-renuka-adi-mathura-alokanam — the sight of the forest of Agra, Renuka and the rest, and of Mathura; tatha — likewise.

3the darshan of Lord Madhava at Prayaga2; the way along the Yamuna; the forest of Agra, Renuka and other places, and Mathura;

Verse 4

कृष्णदासेन च समं घट्टकूपादिदर्शनम्।
वृन्दारण्यादिकं सर्वं द्वादशवनमेव च॥४॥

kṛṣṇadāsena ca samaṁ ghaṭṭakūpādidarśanam|
vṛndāraṇyādikaṁ sarvaṁ dvādaśavanameva ca||4||

krishnadasena — with Krishnadasa; cha — and; samam — together; ghatta-kupa-adi-darshanam — the seeing of ghats, wells and so on; vrindaranya-adikam — Vrindaranya and the rest; sarvam — all; dvadasha-vanam — the twelve forests; eva cha — and.

4the ghats, wells and other holy places that He visited with Krishnadasa; Vrindaranya and all the twelve forests;

Verse 5

प्रतिग्रामं प्रतिवनं प्रतिकुण्डं सनातनम्।
कृष्णनानाप्रकाशञ्च लीलानुकरणं तथा॥५॥

pratigrāmaṁ prativanaṁ pratikuṇḍaṁ sanātanam|
kṛṣṇanānāprakāśañca līlānukaraṇaṁ tathā||5||

prati-gramam — in every village; prati-vanam — in every forest; prati-kundam — at every pond; sanatanam — eternal; krishna-nana-prakasham — the manifold manifestation of Krishna; cha — and; lila-anukaranam — the re-enacting of the pastimes; tatha — likewise.

5in every village, in every forest, at every pond, the eternal and manifold manifestation of Krishna, and the re-enacting of His pastimes;

Verse 6

कृष्णजन्म समारभ्य तथा कंसवधादिकम्।
वर्णनं श्रवणञ्चापि तत्तद्रूपप्रकाशनम्॥६॥

kṛṣṇajanma samārabhya tathā kaṁsavadhādikam|
varṇanaṁ śravaṇañcāpi tattadrūpaprakāśanam||6||

krishna-janma — Krishna's birth; samarabhya — beginning from; tatha — and; kamsa-vadha-adikam — the slaying of Kamsa and the rest; varnanam — the telling; shravanam — the hearing; cha api — and also; tat-tad-rupa-prakashanam — the manifestation of each of those forms.

6the telling and the hearing, from Krishna's birth to the slaying of Kamsa and the rest, and the manifestation of each of those forms;

Verse 7

भावोन्मादविकारादिवर्णनं परमाद्भुतम्।
सर्वव्रजनिवासिनां गृहे गृहे प्रकाशनम्॥७॥

bhāvonmādavikārādivarṇanaṁ paramādbhutam|
sarvavrajanivāsināṁ gṛhe gṛhe prakāśanam||7||

bhava-unmada-vikara-adi-varnanam — the description of the madness of love, its transformations and the rest; parama-adbhutam — most wondrous; sarva-vraja-nivasinam — of all the dwellers of Vraja; grihe grihe — in house after house; prakashanam — the manifestation.

7the most wondrous description of His madness of love, its transformations and the rest; His manifestation in the home of every dweller of Vraja;

Verse 8

पुनरागमनञ्चैव प्रयागे रूपमेलनम्।
काश्यां सनातनस्यापि तपनाद्यनुरोधतः॥८॥

punarāgamanañcaiva prayāge rūpamelanam|
kāśyāṁ sanātanasyāpi tapanādyanurodhataḥ||8||

punah-agamanam — the return; cha eva — and; prayage — at Prayaga; rupa-melanam — the meeting with Rupa; kashyam — at Kashi; sanatanasya — with Sanatana; api — also; tapana-adi-anurodhatah — at the request of Tapana and others.

8the return; the meeting with Rupa at Prayaga and with Sanatana at Kashi; and, at the request of Tapana and others,

Verse 9

काशीवासिजनोद्धारचरितं किल्बिषापहम्।
तक्रपानञ्च गोपस्य नवद्वीपशुभागमः॥९॥

kāśīvāsijanoddhāracaritaṁ kilbiṣāpaham|
takrapānañca gopasya navadvīpaśubhāgamaḥ||9||

kashi-vasi-jana-uddhara-charitam — the story of the deliverance of the people of Kashi; kilbisha-apaham — which removes sin; takra-panam — the drinking of buttermilk; cha — and; gopasya — from a cowherd; navadvipa-shubha-agamah — the auspicious coming to Navadvipa.

9the story of the deliverance of the people of Kashi, which removes sin; how He drank buttermilk from a cowherd; the auspicious coming to Navadvipa;

Verse 10

तत्र नित्यविहारञ्च गौरीदासगृहेऽपि च।
पुनराचार्यगेहे च गमनं शुभदर्शनम्॥१०॥

tatra nityavihārañca gaurīdāsagṛhe'pi ca|
punarācāryagehe ca gamanaṁ śubhadarśanam||10||

tatra — there; nitya-viharam — the eternal pastimes; cha — and; gauridasa-grihe — in Gauridasa's house; api cha — also; punah — then; acharya-gehe — to the Acharya's (Advaita's) house; cha — and; gamanam — the coming; shubha-darshanam — the auspicious meeting.

10the eternal pastimes there and in the house of Gauridasa3; then the coming to the Acharya's house and the auspicious meeting;

Verse 11

भक्तवर्गरसोल्लासो मातुश्चरणवन्दनम्।
माधवाराधनं तत्र नीलाद्रिगमनं ततः॥११॥

bhaktavargarasollāso mātuścaraṇavandanam|
mādhavārādhanaṁ tatra nīlādrigamanaṁ tataḥ||11||

bhakta-varga-rasa-ullasah — the devotees' rapture in rasa; matuh — of the mother; charana-vandanam — the worship of the feet; madhava-aradhanam — the honouring of Madhava (Puri); tatra — there; niladri-gamanam — the going to Niladri; tatah — then.

11the devotees' rapture in rasa; the worship of His mother's feet; the honouring of Madhava Puri4; then the departure for Niladri;

Verse 12

प्रतापरुद्रसन्त्राणं रथयात्रादिदर्शनम्।
नरेन्द्रसरसि भक्तमेलनं हरिकीर्तनम्॥१२॥

pratāparudrasantrāṇaṁ rathayātrādidarśanam|
narendrasarasi bhaktamelanaṁ harikīrtanam||12||

prataparudra-santranam — the deliverance of Prataparudra; ratha-yatra-adi-darshanam — the sight of the Ratha-yatra and the rest; narendra-sarasi — at Narendra Lake; bhakta-melanam — the meeting with the devotees; hari-kirtanam — the kirtana of Hari.

12the deliverance of Prataparudra; the sight of the Ratha-yatra and other festivals; the meeting with the devotees at Narendra Lake and the kirtana of Hari;

Verse 13

तैर्दत्तं भोजनञ्चापि गौराङ्गगुणकीर्तनम्।
कृतमद्वैतप्रभुणा रामदासानुकम्पनम्॥१३॥

tairdattaṁ bhojanañcāpi gaurāṅgaguṇakīrtanam|
kṛtamadvaitaprabhuṇā rāmadāsānukampanam||13||

taih — by them; dattam — given; bhojanam — the meal; cha api — and also; gauranga-guna-kirtanam — the singing of Gauranga's qualities; kritam — done; advaita-prabhuna — by Advaita Prabhu; ramadasa-anukampanam — the mercy to Ramadasa.

13the meal served by the devotees, and the singing of Gauranga's qualities begun by Advaita Prabhu; the mercy to Ramadasa5;

Verse 14

नित्यानन्दविहारादि गौराङ्गगुणकीर्तनम्।
दिव्योन्मादादिभावानां प्राकट्यं स्यादनन्तरम्॥१४॥

nityānandavihārādi gaurāṅgaguṇakīrtanam|
divyonmādādibhāvānāṁ prākaṭyaṁ syādanantaram||14||

nityananda-vihara-adi — Nityananda's pastimes and so on; gauranga-guna-kirtanam — the singing of Gauranga's qualities; divya-unmada-adi-bhavanam — of divine madness and other states; prakatyam — the manifestation; syat — was; anantaram — next.

14Nityananda's pastimes and the rest, the singing of Gauranga's qualities; then the manifestation of divine madness and other states;

Verse 15

रामानन्दस्वरूपाद्यै राससंकीर्तनादिकम्।
नित्यानन्दविहारादिवर्णनं गौरदर्शनम्॥१५॥

rāmānandasvarūpādyai rāsasaṁkīrtanādikam|
nityānandavihārādivarṇanaṁ gauradarśanam||15||

ramananda-svarupa-adyaih — by Ramananda, Svarupa and others; rasa-sankirtana-adikam — the singing of the rasa-lila and the like; nityananda-vihara-adi-varnanam — the description of Nityananda's pastimes and so on; gaura-darshanam — the meeting with Gaura.

15the singing of the rasa-lila and the like by Ramananda, Svarupa and others; the description of Nityananda's pastimes and so on; His meeting with Gaura;

Verse 16

गुण्डिचायां पुष्पवाट्यां विराजञ्च सभक्तयोः।
गदाधरसमं नित्यानन्दगौराङ्गचन्द्रयोः॥१६॥

guṇḍicāyāṁ puṣpavāṭyāṁ virājañca sabhaktayoḥ|
gadādharasamaṁ nityānandagaurāṅgacandrayoḥ||16||

gundichayam — at Gundicha; pushpa-vatyam — in the flower garden; virajam — the splendour; cha — and; sa-bhaktayoh — of the two with Their devotees; gadadhara-samam — together with Gadadhara; nityananda-gauranga-chandrayoh — of Nityananda and Gaurangachandra.

16and the splendour of Nityananda and Gaurangachandra, surrounded by Their devotees, together with Gadadhara, in the flower garden at Gundicha.

Verse 17

एवं सञ्चिन्तयन् कृष्णचैतन्यचरितं बुधः।
शुद्धप्रेमामृतनिधौ निमग्नो भवति सदा॥१७॥

evaṁ sañcintayan kṛṣṇacaitanyacaritaṁ budhaḥ|
śuddhapremāmṛtanidhau nimagno bhavati sadā||17||

evam — thus; sanchintayan — contemplating; krishna-chaitanya-charitam — the life of Krishna Chaitanya; budhah — the wise one; shuddha-prema-amrita-nidhau — in the ocean of the nectar of pure prema; nimagnah — immersed; bhavati — becomes; sada — forever.

17Contemplating thus the life of Krishna Chaitanya, the wise are immersed forever in the ocean of the nectar of pure prema.

Verse 18

ईश्वरोऽपि स्वयं कृष्णो यतो भक्तिरसाश्रयः।
आस्वादयति स्वप्रेमनाममाधुर्यमद्भुतम्॥१८॥

īśvaro'pi svayaṁ kṛṣṇo yato bhaktirasāśrayaḥ|
āsvādayati svapremanāmamādhuryamadbhutam||18||

ishvarah — the Lord; api — though; svayam — Himself; krishnah — Krishna; yatah — since; bhakti-rasa-ashrayah — the abode of the rasa of bhakti; asvadayati — tastes; sva-prema-nama-madhuryam — the sweetness of love for Himself and of His Name; adbhutam — wondrous.

18For Krishna Himself, though He is the Lord, is the abode (ashraya) of the rasa of bhakti6, and tastes the wondrous sweetness of love for Himself and of His own Name.

Verse 19

तल्लीलास्वादनादेव किं न स्यात् प्रेमवैभवम्।
अतो निर्मत्सरो भूत्वा शृणु गौराङ्गकीर्तनम्॥१९॥

tallīlāsvādanādeva kiṁ na syāt premavaibhavam|
ato nirmatsaro bhūtvā śṛṇu gaurāṅgakīrtanam||19||

tal-lila-asvadanat — from tasting His pastimes; eva — indeed; kim na syat — what would not arise; prema-vaibhavam — the splendour of prema; atah — therefore; nirmatsarah — free from envy; bhutva — becoming; shrinu — hear; gauranga-kirtanam — the glorification of Gauranga.

19What splendour of prema would not arise from simply tasting His pastimes? Therefore, casting off envy, hear the glorification of Gauranga.

Verse 20

चत्वारः प्रक्रमा अस्य सर्गादि अष्टसप्ततिः।
प्रथमः षोडशश्चापि द्वितीयोऽष्टादशस्तथा॥२०॥

catvāraḥ prakramā asya sargādi aṣṭasaptatiḥ|
prathamaḥ ṣoḍaśaścāpi dvitīyo'ṣṭādaśastathā||20||

chatvarah — four; prakramah — prakramas; asya — of it (the poem); sarga-adi — of sargas; ashta-saptatih — seventy-eight; prathamah — the first; shodashah — sixteen; cha api — and; dvitiyah — the second; ashtadashah — eighteen; tatha — likewise.

20This poem has four prakramas and seventy-eight sargas: the first has sixteen, the second eighteen,

Verse 21

तृतीयस्तु तथैव स्यात् चतुर्थः षड्विंशतिः।
एकोनविंशशतशः सप्तविंशाधिकानि च॥२१॥

tṛtīyastu tathaiva syāt caturthaḥ ṣaḍviṁśatiḥ|
ekonaviṁśaśataśaḥ saptaviṁśādhikāni ca||21||

tritiyah — the third; tu — and; tatha eva — likewise; syat — is; chaturthah — the fourth; shad-vimshatih — twenty-six; ekonavimsha-shatashah — nineteen hundreds; sapta-vimsha-adhikani — with twenty-seven more; cha — and.

21the third the same, the fourth twenty-six; and the verses number nineteen hundred and twenty-seven7.

Verse 22

श्लोकानि सुपठन्नेव रसिकः परमादरात्।
प्रेमपूर्णो भवेन्नित्यं श्रवणादपि भावुकः॥२२॥

ślokāni supaṭhanneva rasikaḥ paramādarāt|
premapūrṇo bhavennityaṁ śravaṇādapi bhāvukaḥ||22||

shlokani — the verses; supathan — reciting well; eva — indeed; rasikah — a lover of rasa; parama-adarat — with the greatest reverence; prema-purnah — full of prema; bhavet — will become; nityam — forever; shravanat — by hearing; api — even; bhavukah — one of feeling heart.

22A lover of rasa who reads these verses with the greatest reverence will be forever filled with prema — and so will one of feeling heart, even by hearing them.

Verse 23

श्रुत्वा सर्वं नित्यानन्दगौराङ्गगुणकीर्तनम्।
मुरारिं सम्प्रणम्याह श्रीदामोदरपण्डितः॥२३॥

śrutvā sarvaṁ nityānandagaurāṅgaguṇakīrtanam|
murāriṁ sampraṇamyāha śrīdāmodarapaṇḍitaḥ||23||

shrutva — having heard; sarvam — all; nityananda-gauranga-guna-kirtanam — the glorification of the qualities of Nityananda and Gauranga; murarim — to Murari; sampranamya — bowing; aha — said; shri-damodara-panditah — Sri Damodara Pandita.

23Having heard all this glorification of the qualities of Nityananda and Gauranga, Sri Damodara Pandita bowed to Murari and said:

Verse 24

कृतार्थोऽहं कृतार्थोऽहं कृतार्थोऽहं न संशयः।
धन्योऽसि हि भवान् कृष्णचैतन्यरसपूरकः॥२४॥

kṛtārtho'haṁ kṛtārtho'haṁ kṛtārtho'haṁ na saṁśayaḥ|
dhanyo'si hi bhavān kṛṣṇacaitanyarasapūrakaḥ||24||

krita-arthah — fulfilled; aham — I; na samshayah — there is no doubt; dhanyah — blessed; asi — are; hi — truly; bhavan — you; krishna-chaitanya-rasa-purakah — who fill (hearts) with the rasa of Krishna Chaitanya.

24"I have reached my goal, I have reached my goal, I have reached my goal — of this there is no doubt! Blessed are you, who fill hearts with the rasa of Krishna Chaitanya!"

Verse 25

श्रीलाद्वैतप्रभुरपि सुखं श्रीलगौराङ्गचन्द्र-
लीलारत्नसमञ्जसं सुमधुरमाश्रुत्य हर्षादसौ।
तं प्राह श्रीमुरारिं त्वमपि खलु सदा रामचन्द्रस्य […]
तस्मादेतत्त्वयि प्रकटितं ग्रन्थरत्नं हि तेन॥२५॥

śrīlādvaitaprabhurapi sukhaṁ śrīlagaurāṅgacandra-
līlāratnasamañjasaṁ sumadhuramāśrutya harṣādasau|
taṁ prāha śrīmurāriṁ tvamapi khalu sadā rāmacandrasya […]
tasmādetattvayi prakaṭitaṁ grantharatnaṁ hi tena||25||

shrila-advaita-prabhuh — Srila Advaita Prabhu; api — also; sukham — joyfully; shrila-gauranga-chandra-lila-ratna-samanjasam — the well-ordered string of jewels of Srila Gaurangachandra's pastimes; su-madhuram — most sweet; ashrutya — having heard; harshat — in delight; asau — he; tam — to him; praha — said; shri-murarim — to Sri Murari; tvam — you; api khalu — indeed; sada — always; ramachandrasya — of Ramachandra […]; tasmat — therefore; etat — this; tvayi — in you; prakatitam — has been revealed; grantha-ratnam — jewel of a book; hi — indeed; tena — by Him.

25Srila Advaita Prabhu too, having joyfully heard this most sweet, well-ordered string of jewels of Srila Gaurangachandra's pastimes, said in delight to Sri Murari, "You are ever [devoted] to Ramachandra8; that is why He has revealed through you this jewel of a book.

Verse 26

श्रीरामो गौर इह जगति प्रादुरासीद्यतोऽसौ
ग्रन्थेनैतेन जनयति हि प्रेममाधुर्यसारम्।
श्रुत्वा सर्वे परमरसिकाः प्रेमपूर्णान्तराश्च
गायन्तस्तं परमसुखदं मोक्षमेवाक्षिपन्ति॥२६॥

śrīrāmo gaura iha jagati prādurāsīdyato'sau
granthenaitena janayati hi premamādhuryasāram|
śrutvā sarve paramarasikāḥ premapūrṇāntarāśca
gāyantastaṁ paramasukhadaṁ mokṣamevākṣipanti||26||

shri-ramah — Sri Rama; gaurah — as Gaura; iha — here; jagati — in the world; pradurasit — has appeared; yatah — since; asau — He; granthena — through book; etena — this; janayati — brings forth; hi — indeed; prema-madhurya-saram — the essence of the sweetness of prema; shrutva — hearing; sarve — all; parama-rasikah — the highest connoisseurs of rasa; prema-purna-antarah — their hearts full of prema; cha — and; gayantah — singing; tam — of Him; parama-sukha-dam — the giver of the highest bliss; moksham — liberation; eva — even; akshipanti — cast aside.

26For this Sri Rama has appeared in the world as Gaura9, and through this book He brings forth the very essence of the sweetness of prema. Hearing it, all the highest connoisseurs of rasa, their hearts full of prema, sing of Him, the giver of the highest bliss, and cast aside even liberation."

Verse 27

श्रीवासपण्डितः प्राह प्रेमगद्गदया गिरा।
ग्रन्थमासाद्य हर्षेण मुरारिं परमोत्सुकः॥२७॥

śrīvāsapaṇḍitaḥ prāha premagadgadayā girā|
granthamāsādya harṣeṇa murāriṁ paramotsukaḥ||27||

shrivasa-panditah — Srivasa Pandita; praha — said; prema-gadgadaya — choked with love; gira — in a voice; grantham — the book; asadya — receiving; harshena — with joy; murarim — to Murari; parama-utsukah — most eager.

27Srivasa Pandita, receiving the book, joyful and most eager, said to Murari in a voice choked with love:

Verse 28

त्वमेव जगतां बन्धमोक्षाय कृतवान् हरेः।
लीलां भगवतो ग्रन्थं श्रुत्वा मुच्येज्जनो भयात्॥२८॥

tvameva jagatāṁ bandhamokṣāya kṛtavān hareḥ|
līlāṁ bhagavato granthaṁ śrutvā mucyejjano bhayāt||28||

tvam eva — you indeed; jagatam — of the worlds; bandha-mokshaya — for release from bondage; kritavan — have made; hareh — of Hari; lilam — the pastimes; bhagavatah — of Bhagavan; grantham — into a book; shrutva — hearing; muchyet — will be freed; janah — a person; bhayat — from fear.

28"It is you who, to free the worlds from bondage, have set down in a book the pastimes of Hari, Bhagavan: hearing it, a person will be freed from fear."10

Verse 29

एवं भक्तगणाः सर्वे ग्रन्थवर्णनमद्भुतम्।
श्रुत्वा मुरारिं संनम्य प्राहुस्तस्य कथा मिथः॥२९॥

evaṁ bhaktagaṇāḥ sarve granthavarṇanamadbhutam|
śrutvā murāriṁ saṁnamya prāhustasya kathā mithaḥ||29||

evam — thus; bhakta-ganah — the devotees; sarve — all; grantha-varnanam — the narrative of the book; adbhutam — wondrous; shrutva — having heard; murarim — to Murari; sannamya — bowing; prahuh — spoke; tasya — his; kathah — tales; mithah — to one another.

29Thus all the devotees, having heard the wondrous narrative of the book, bowed to Murari and spoke among themselves of his tale.

Verse 30

सोऽपि प्रणम्य विधिवन्मुरारि-
र्धृत्वा तु तेषां चरणारविन्दम्।
प्रेम्णा जय कृष्णचैतन्यराम
इति ब्रुवन्नृत्यति रोरवीति॥३०॥

so'pi praṇamya vidhivanmurāri-
rdhṛtvā tu teṣāṁ caraṇāravindam|
premṇā jaya kṛṣṇacaitanyarāma
iti bruvannṛtyati roravīti||30||

sah — he; api — too; pranamya — bowing; vidhivat — duly; murarih — Murari; dhritva — clasping; tu — and; tesham — their; charana-aravindam — lotus feet; premna — with love; jaya — glory; krishna-chaitanya-rama — to Krishna Chaitanya and Rama; iti — thus; bruvan — crying; nrityati — dances; roraviti — cries aloud.

30And Murari, duly bowing to them and clasping their lotus feet, cries out with love, "Glory to Krishna Chaitanya and Rama!"11 — and dances and calls aloud.

Verse 31

अन्योन्यमालिङ्ग्य च श्रीगौरचन्द्र-
रसेन पूर्णाः किल ते बभूवुः।
श्रीपतिरेकेन जगद्धिताय
प्रकाश्य लीलां सुरहस्यमेतत्॥३१॥

anyonyamāliṅgya ca śrīgauracandra-
rasena pūrṇāḥ kila te babhūvuḥ|
śrīpatirekena jagaddhitāya
prakāśya līlāṁ surahasyametat||31||

anyonyam — one another; alingya — embracing; cha — and; shri-gaurachandra-rasena — with the rasa of Sri Gaurachandra; purnah — filled; kila — truly; te — they; babhuvuh — became; shri-patih — Shripati (the Lord of Sri); ekena — through one; jagat-hitaya — for the good of the world; prakashya — revealing; lilam — the pastimes; su-rahasyam — a deep secret; etat — this.

31Embracing one another, they were all filled with the rasa of Sri Gaurachandra: "Through one man Shripati has revealed His pastimes for the good of the world — this is a deep secret!"12

Verse 32

चतुर्दशशताब्दान्ते पञ्चत्रिंशतिवत्सरे।
आषाढसितसप्तम्यां ग्रन्थोऽयं पूर्णतां गतः॥३२॥

caturdaśaśatābdānte pañcatriṁśativatsare|
āṣāḍhasitasaptamyāṁ grantho'yaṁ pūrṇatāṁ gataḥ||32||

chaturdasha-shatabda-ante — at the end of fourteen hundred years; pancha-trimshati-vatsare — in the thirty-fifth year; ashadha-sita-saptamyam — on the seventh day of the bright half of Ashadha; granthah — book; ayam — this; purnatam — completion; gatah — reached.

32This book was completed at the end of fourteen hundred years, in the thirty-fifth year, on the seventh day of the bright half of the month of Ashadha13.

Thus ends the twenty-sixth sarga of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita." The book is complete.

Notes

  1. Vishveshvara: Shiva, the lord of Kashi; Tapana: Tapana Mishra (cf. 4.13).
  2. Veni-Madhava, the Deity of the Lord at Prayaga.
  3. In the house of Gauridasa Pandita, Gaura and Nityananda manifested Themselves in Deities and eternally reside there (4.14).
  4. Madhavendra Puri, the guru of Ishvara Puri, on the day of his remembrance (4.15).
  5. See 4.21 and the note on its colophon.
  6. That is, He takes the position of a devotee, as Sri Chaitanya, to taste the sweetness His devotees taste (cf. 4.24.11).
  7. In the edition's numbering followed in this translation there are 1,926 verses.
  8. Murari is a devotee of Ramachandra (cf. 2.07, where the Lord calls him Ramadasa). The manuscripts have a gap here; the word "devoted" is supplied from the sense.
  9. To Murari, a devotee of Ramachandra, Gaura revealed Himself as Rama. Gaura is Krishna Himself, the source of all avataras, and Ramachandra too is present in Him.
  10. Freedom from the bonds of material existence and from fear is only a by-product of hearing this book; its highest fruit is prema, for whose sake the true connoisseurs of rasa cast aside even liberation (vv. 22, 26).
  11. Rama: Nityananda-Rama (Balarama); cf. 4.24.30.
  12. Shripati, "the Consort of Sri (Lakshmi)," is a name of the Lord. The sense of the verse is not entirely clear; "through one man" probably means through Murari.
  13. That is, in the year 1435, apparently of the Shaka era, which is 1513 CE; the bright half of Ashadha falls in June–July. This date is earlier than some of the events the poem describes (the journey to Vrindavana and what follows), so its relation to the final text of the poem is unclear.
